ai.title: LinkedIn ID propagation in Stripe checkout URLs
ai.summary: Stripe checkout success and cancel URLs now preserve LinkedIn `li_fat_id` and UTM parameters via `searchParams` in `web/src/app/api/stripe/checkout-session/route.ts`. `trackUpgrade` in `web/src/lib/trackConversions.ts` replaces `trackUpgradeClick`, conditionally firing `linkedInTrack` only on final conversion to prevent premature attribution loss. `web/src/app/payment-success/page.tsx` merges these params back into the URL using `router.replace`. Credit display values in `npm-app/src/client.ts` and `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` now use `toLocaleString()`.

eli5.text: When you click through to sign up for Codebuff Pro on Stripe, the special link used to track where you came from (like LinkedIn ads or campaign tags) used to get dropped off before reaching the payment page. Now those tracking details stay attached all the way through checkout and back to the success page. You won't see a visual difference, but behind the scenes your visit will be correctly credited in analytics, so marketing efforts are measured accurately. This applies to anyone who lands on the pricing or payment pages via tracked links, and it's live now.

ai.title: Add indexes for message userid and fingerprintid
ai.summary: Added btree indexes on `message.user_id` and `message.fingerprint_id` to speed up usage calculations. Defined in `common/src/db/schema.ts` and applied via migration `0009_bitter_rumiko_fujikawa.sql`. Updated `schema.knowledge.md` with guidelines on index management and performance.

eli5.text: The system now files messages in two new organizational drawers, one labeled by who sent them and one by where they came from. This is the kind of thing you'd notice as faster loading when looking up usage history tied to a specific person or connection, because the computer no longer has to flip through every message to find the right ones.

ai.title: CLI shows last request credits
ai.summary: CLI displays credits used for the last request when `lastRequestCredits` exceeds `REQUEST_CREDIT_SHOW_THRESHOLD`. Client calculates per-request usage by tracking the delta between total session credits in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Logic updates `common/src/constants.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to gate the message visibility.

eli5.text: After you run a request, the tool now tells you how many credits that single request cost, as long as the cost is more than one credit. The system figures this out by remembering how many total credits you had before and subtracting that from the new total it receives, so you see a per-request cost rather than just a running sum.
